newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific BBA sees substantial earnings lift.
newsitem.headline: Pacific BBA sees substantial earnings lift.

text.p: Manufacturing group Pacific BBA Ltd said on Wednesday it saw a substantial increase in its earnings in calendar 1997.

Asked by reporters what was the magnitude of the earnings rise the company expected for its year results, chairman Barry Jackson said: "It will be substantial, but it is too early to be positive about how much."
Jackson said the company expected most of earnings growth to come from its Asian operations as well as export growth from Australia of automotive parts, mainly to the U.S.
The company was speaking to a number of interested parties to invest in its brake parts plant, currently being built in Tennessee, he said.
"We are not in any rush. We would rather get the plant finished and commissioned before we have a partner to keep informed and give the details to," he said.
Jackson said the company was close to signing a joint venture deal for a new webforge plant in China and an announcement was expected soon.
Pacific BBA reported a net profit of A$16.87 million for calendar 1996.
Pacific BBA shares were six cents firmer at A$4.76 at 12.20 p.m. (0220 GMT) on Wednesday.
